narrow_reads: count: table + size*8, low two bytes
symbol: table + 128 + ordinal*8, low two bytes
cursor/end at offsets 0/32, low two bytes; reservoir/available/failed at 8/16/24, low one byte
narrow_writes: cursor at 0, low two bytes; reservoir/available/failed at 8/16/24, low one byte; remaining already-zero high bytes unchanged

private_state_induction.bit_reader_failure: Unchanged f4 b6 commits only the whole-u64 failed flag=1; it does not commit partially-refilled local reservoir, availability or cursor. Persisted values and their six zero high bytes remain unchanged.
private_state_induction.bit_reader_success: Unchanged f4 refills only while available<n; n<=16. It commits reservoir shifted by n, remaining available<=7, cursor<=63632 through complete-u64 f3 writes.
private_state_induction.initial_state: Unchanged f0 b8 clears all [0,8192) before any decoding, writes whole-u64 cursor 8192 and end 63632 through unchanged f3.
private_state_induction.installation: Unchanged f10/f11..f17 write only compressed bytes [8192,63632) and whole-u64 cursor; f0 resets cursor to 8192 before f9.
private_state_induction.mutable_borrow_contract: Input/output/workspace are disjoint, stable borrows for the synchronous public f0 call; arbitrary direct f6 entry and concurrent external state mutation are not this public ABI.
private_state_induction.other_state_writer: Unchanged f9 stored-block alignment writes whole-u64 zero to reservoir/available; no table/output/compressed writer aliases state offsets [0,40).
private_state_induction.representation: Cursor/end fit u16; persisted reservoir<256, availability<=7, failed<=1 fit u8 before every f6 read. f4 refills into local variables only, and its failure branch does not commit them. Complete-u64 writers and bounded narrow writes inductively preserve all six/seven omitted zero high bytes.
private_state_induction.symbol_failure: If failed was already set, f6 preserves bit state. EOF or no-code sets failed=1; the other state retains the same bounds. Cursor low-two-byte and reservoir/availability/failed low-one-byte writes preserve all already-zero high bytes.
private_state_induction.symbol_success: f6 consumes at most one bit at a time, refills one byte only when availability is zero and cursor<end; commits position<=63632, reservoir<256, available<=7, failed<=1.
